LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 2.1.1 ORAL PRESENTATIONS: SONGS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.1: Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs, part of Strand 2 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can one improve the presentation of a song to make it interesting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify features of songs in the locality,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use performance techniques when singing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. write songs on a scientific innovation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the role of songs in the society.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify features of songs in the locality,

   Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. use performance techniques when singing,

   Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. write songs on a scientific innovation,

   Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate the role of songs in the society.

   Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. watch recordings of songs from the Kenya drama and music festivals,

2. discuss the performance techniques that make the presentations appealing and make notes,

3. identify songs of their choice and present them to the rest of the class,

4. write songs on scientific innovations,

5. collaborate to recite and record the songs or poems,

6. watch the recordings and discuss the non- verbal aspects of the performance.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. watch recordings of songs from the Kenya drama and music festivals,
2. discuss the performance techniques that make the presentations appealing and make notes,
3. identify songs of their choice and present them to the rest of the class,
4. write songs on scientific innovations,
5. collaborate to recite and record the songs or poems,
6. watch the recordings and discuss the non- verbal aspects of the performance.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and imagination: This is enhanced as the learner writes songs on scientific innovations.

• Digital literacy: It is enhanced as the learner uses digital devices to record and watch performances then discuss non-verbal

aspects of performances.

Values:
Patriotism: It is fostered as the learner appreciates their culture while singing the different uniting songs.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: It is fostered as the learner watches Drama and Music Festival performances from different communities fostering

social cohesion and patriotism.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to apply the skills acquired in drama performance techniques to Creative arts and sports.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify features of songs in the locality,
2. use performance techniques when singing,
3. write songs on a scientific innovation,
4. appreciate the role of songs in the society.

Remember the key question: How can one improve the presentation of a song to make it interesting?
